root: ^  Your body protests the endless marching. Each step becomes a struggle.
^  Your legs grow heavy with fatigue, but you push onward.
^  The march continues, though your legs grow heavy.
^The year is {gameState.year}. The war between England and France has just begun.
^  {gameState.characterName}, you are a {gameState.culture || ""} man, ready to make your mark on history.
^  You are a soldier, ready to make your mark on history.
^The training master eyes you up and down. "Let's see what you're made of," he grunts.
^  Your muscular frame suggests you've done hard labor before.
^  Your slight build concerns the training master.
^  You have an average build for a soldier.
^  You adjust your shield, feeling its familiar weight.
^  Your hands feel empty without a shield.
^Your basic training is complete. The training master nods in approval.
^"You've learned the basics," he says. "But the real test awaits on the battlefield."
^  Your strength will serve you well in combat.
^  You'll need to rely on more than just brute strength.
^  Your tactical mind gives you an edge.
^You arrive at the army encampment. Tents stretch as far as the eye can see, and the air is thick with anticipation.
^A sergeant approaches you. "New recruit? We're preparing for the campaign. You'll need proper equipment."
^The quartermaster eyes you critically. "Equipment costs money, and you don't look like you have much."
^  "You've got enough for decent gear. What's your choice?"
^  "Barely enough for basic equipment. Choose wisely."
^  "You're short on funds. Maybe start with something cheap."
^The quartermaster hands you your equipment. "Take care of it - it might save your life."
^The bounty board is covered in notices from commanders seeking soldiers for various tasks.
^  "Strong fighters wanted for heavy infantry duty."
^  "Scouts needed - agility more important than strength."
^  "Tactical officers wanted - must be able to read and write."
^  "Basic infantry needed - no special skills required."
^You find a spot by the campfire where soldiers are sharing stories and rations.
^  The camaraderie lifts your spirits. You feel ready for whatever comes next.
^  You keep to yourself, watching the others warily.
^  You listen quietly, taking in the atmosphere of military life.
^  Your exhaustion makes it hard to enjoy the moment.
^  You feel relatively rested and engaged.
^You share a tale from your hometown. The soldiers listen appreciatively.
^  Your storytelling captivates the audience. Even the sergeant nods in approval.
^  Your story is received politely, if not enthusiastically.
^You listen to the veterans speak of battles past. Their experience is valuable education.
^  You quickly grasp the tactical lessons they're sharing.
^  Some of the talk goes over your head, but you learn what you can.
^You find a quiet spot to rest. The warmth of the fire soothes your tired muscles.
^  The rest helps, but you're still wound tight from recent exertions.
^  You feel genuinely refreshed by the break.
^You join the heavy infantry. The armor is heavy, but the protection is worth it.
^  You handle the heavy equipment well. The drill master nods in approval.
^  You struggle with the weight, but determination sees you through.
^  Your shield feels natural in the tight formation.
^  You feel vulnerable without a shield in the press of bodies.
^Your light frame serves you well as a scout. Speed and stealth are your allies.
^  You move through the terrain with natural grace.
^  The work is challenging, but you're learning quickly.
^The officer training is demanding. Reading, writing, and tactical thinking are required.
^  You grasp the tactical concepts quickly.
^  You struggle but manage to keep up.
^  The material is difficult, but you're determined to learn.
^The road to Calais is long and muddy. The army moves as one massive organism.
^  This is the year of the great chevauchée - the raid that will scar Normandy.
^  The campaign continues toward its objective.
^  Every step is agony. Your body screams for rest, but the army doesn't stop.
^  The march grinds on your nerves, but you hold your place in line.
^  You maintain steady pace, conserving energy for what lies ahead.
^Calais appears on the horizon. The siege is about to begin.
^  The Calais chapter of your life begins now.
^Your journey has transformed you from a raw recruit into a seasoned soldier.
^  Your strength has grown through hardship.
^  You've learned that strength isn't everything.
^  Your mind is sharper now, honed by experience.
^  Experience has been your greatest teacher.
^You look back on the journey that brought you here.
^  Your reputation precedes you. Soldiers recognize your name.
^  You've made some enemies along the way.
^  You're still building your reputation in this army.
